last_assistant_message:
Full primary report resent to the coordinator in the requested three-bucket structure (adoption stats / deployed-in-production / emerging-governance), with claim, number, company, source name, URL, date, and confidence note per item, plus the do-NOT-use list.

Summary of what was delivered across all messages:
- **Full primary report** (just sent) — 54 sourced items across the three buckets plus an 11-item do-NOT-use list.
- **Addendum** — additional Category 2 products (Amazon Connect Talent, HackerRank Chakra, Textio Lavalier, Pete & Gabi, micro1, HeyMilo, Sapia.ai, Joveo), named employers (Xponential Fitness, Chipotle, McDonald's, Fontainebleau, Olive Garden, US federal pilot), the Paradox password-exposure incident, and governance additions (California No Robo Bosses Act, CVS settlement).
- **Correction** — Colorado AI Act: SB 24-205 repealed/replaced by SB 26-189; applies to consequential decisions on/after Jan 1, 2027.

Note on the two still-running parallel researchers (Categories 3 and 4): their domains are fully covered in the primary report I just resent, so nothing is missing from the deliverable. If they return new material, it would be duplicative.

One standing caveat for the deck: the sharpest, most defensible "emerging frontier" story is Workday's (agents, MCP, Anthropic/Sana, C1.ai agent-identity) — but almost all of it is early-access or announced, with only a handful of broadly-GA products. The governance slide's strongest non-obvious point is the 2026 split: the federal EEOC deprioritized disparate-impact enforcement while California, Colorado, and the EU AI Act tightened automated-hiring rules.
